title: Things I built. Things I actually care about.

items.title: SprintDesk
items.overview: Software teams have no shortage of sprint tracking tools, but many are too heavy or too disconnected from where the actual work happens. Engineers lose context moving between GitHub, Jira, Slack, and their calendar. I built SprintDesk as a lightweight, real-time Kanban tracker that brings the right context into one place without asking people to change how they already work.
responsibilities: Built a task management app using React 19, TypeScript, and Supabase with a drag-and-drop Kanban board and full sprint cycle tracking.
Designed the component system in Figma before writing code, then used specification-driven prompting with GitHub Copilot to implement directly from design specs.
Built real-time sync with Supabase Realtime so changes appear instantly across users without a refresh.
Implemented per-user data isolation through row-level security so users only see and interact with their own tasks and boards.
Built an activity log recording every task move and update for auditability.
Integrated MCP to connect GitHub, Jira, Slack, and Google Calendar into one workspace.

items.title: Cue
items.overview: Coordinating music rehearsals through group chats creates missed updates, unclear ownership, and too much manual follow-up. As a singer who has dealt with that firsthand, I built Cue as a role-based rehearsal coordination platform for singers and musicians.
responsibilities: Conducted user interviews to understand rehearsal coordination gaps caused by group chats and scattered planning workflows.
Designed wireframes and high-fidelity Figma prototypes using HCI and UX principles to improve rehearsal planning workflows.
Developed a React-based platform with role-aware workflows, structured state management, and synchronized updates using Socket.IO and REST APIs.
Exploring Spotify Web API and Web Playback SDK integrations so users can play rehearsal songs directly inside Cue for smoother preparation.

items.title: Hearing the Battle: How Dynamic Game Audio Shapes Gameplay Experience
items.overview: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang changes battle music during high-pressure gameplay moments, and those audio shifts can shape how players feel momentum, pressure, intensity, and flow. This study examines adaptive battle music as a real-time feedback system from a UX and HCI perspective.
responsibilities: Conducting an independent UX and HCI research study on how adaptive battle music in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang shapes player emotion and gameplay experience.
Creating an observational dataset by tracking how battle background music changes during team fights, enemy wipes, Lord fights, comeback moments, and base-defense situations.
Linking audio transitions to emotional reactions during matches to study how sound affects perceived gameplay momentum and pressure.
Bringing a UX-focused perspective shaped by attention to small design choices and how they influence emotion and experience.
Combining long-term ranked player experience with musical sensitivity as a singer to analyze pacing, rhythm, and emotional shifts in sound.
